## Purpose and setup

Iteration 3. This notebook picks the CH4 model used for the statewide upscaled
estimate, and reports how a more complex, site-level model performs by
comparison. It answers three questions:

1. **Ecoregion model.** How well does `CH4_resp ~ Ecoregion` describe
   site-mean CH4? This is the model used for upscaling.
2. **Fixed or random ecoregion?** Does `CH4_resp ~ 1 + (1 | Ecoregion)` do
   better than ecoregion as a fixed effect? This matters for the five EPA
   Level III ecoregions in New York with no sites (Section 1). A fixed-effect
   model has no coefficient for those areas. A random-effect model predicts
   the population mean there.
3. **Complex model.** How much more does
   `CH4_resp ~ Ecoregion + WETprob_mean * DMV_sd + GEO_modefrac` explain,
   in-sample and out-of-sample? This is the model "fit more directly to the
   data" and is reported alongside the upscaled estimate. It is not used to
   upscale.

Design:

* **Ecoregion:** EPA Level III ecoregion (`US_L3NAME`), from
  `NYDEC_GHG_Sites_EcoEPA_6347.gpkg` via the raster predictor CSV. These are
  the labels of the statewide polygons in `Data/Ecoregions/NY_ECO_L3_6347.gpkg`
  that the upscaling uses. The four sampled EPA ecoregions map one-to-one to
  the original NYDEC strata (`Ecoregion_NYDEC`), so model fits are unchanged
  by the relabel.
* **Response:** site-mean CH4 (mean of the two sampling rounds), n = 48,
  12 sites in each of 4 sampled ecoregions. Modeled as `CH4_resp = log(CH4 + c)`, the
  same transform as `GHG_Dredge.qmd` and `GHG_Model_SiteRanef.qmd`.
* **Covariates:** 10 m window raster statistics, standardized (mean 0, SD 1).
  The scaling constants are saved in `z_scaling` so the upscaling rasters can
  be put on the same scale.
* **Not covered here:** uncertainty in the upscaled estimate, the
  back-transformation from the log scale to mean flux, and wetland area
  weighting. Those come in the next notebook. Predictions below are on the
  model (log) scale. Back-transformed values are medians, not means.

The complex model's structure came out of the all-subsets search in
`GHG_Dredge.qmd`. Cross-validating a fixed formula here leaves out that
selection step, so its cross-validated R² is still somewhat optimistic. The
nested CV in `GHG_Dredge.qmd` is the honest check.

```{r setup}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(here)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest) # p-values for lmer fixed effects (Satterthwaite)
library(MuMIn)    # r.squaredGLMM, AICc

## --- Settings ---------------------------------------------------------------
RASTER_CSV <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Site_RasterPredictors.csv")
SITES_GPKG <- here("Data/GHG/NYDEC_GHG_Sites_EcoEPA_6347.gpkg")
ECO_GPKG <- here("Data/Ecoregions/NY_ECO_L3_6347.gpkg") # EPA Level III, NY

WINDOW <- 10 # raster window (m)

## Covariates of the complex model: short name -> column in RASTER_CSV
COVARIATES <- c(
  WETprob_mean = sprintf("WETprob_mean_%dm", WINDOW),
  DMV_sd       = sprintf("DMV_sd_%dm", WINDOW),
  GEO_modefrac = sprintf("GEO_modefrac_%dm", WINDOW)
)

SHIFT_ADD <- 0.02 # c = |min(CH4)| + SHIFT_ADD (same as GHG_Dredge.qmd)

CV_BLOCK_KM <- 25 # spatial CV: sites grouped within this distance are held out together
NEIGHBOUR_KM <- 25 # Moran's I neighbourhood (Section 7)

set.seed(1)

## --- Plot styling (same palette as the EDA notebook) ------------------------
WT_COLS <- c(EM = "#2a78d6", FO = "#eb6834", SS = "#1baf7a")
WT_SHAPES <- c(EM = 16, FO = 17, SS = 15)
ECO_COLS <- c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#8d5bd6")
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          legend.position = "top")
)
```

## 1. Data

```{r load}
flux_site <- st_read(SITES_GPKG, quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(Site_ID) |>
  summarise(CH4 = mean(CH4_avg), .groups = "drop")

dat <- read.csv(RASTER_CSV, colClasses = c(huc12 = "character")) |>
  select(Site_ID, Ecoregion, US_L3CODE, Ecoregion_NYDEC, Wetland_Type, x, y,
         all_of(unname(COVARIATES))) |>
  left_join(flux_site, by = "Site_ID") |>
  rename(all_of(COVARIATES)) |>
  mutate(
    Ecoregion = factor(Ecoregion),
    Wetland_Type = factor(Wetland_Type, levels = names(WT_COLS)),
    ## standardized copies used in the models: z_<name>
    across(all_of(names(COVARIATES)), \(v) as.numeric(scale(v)), .names = "z_{.col}")
  )

stopifnot(nrow(dat) == 48, !anyNA(dat), nlevels(dat$Ecoregion) == 4)

## Keep the standardization constants for applying the model to rasters
z_scaling <- tibble(covariate = names(COVARIATES), column = unname(COVARIATES),
                    mean = map_dbl(names(COVARIATES), \(v) mean(dat[[v]])),
                    sd = map_dbl(names(COVARIATES), \(v) sd(dat[[v]])))
kable(z_scaling, digits = 4, caption = "Covariate standardization constants (z = (x - mean) / sd)")

table(dat$Ecoregion, dat$Wetland_Type) |>
  kable(caption = "Sites by EPA Level III ecoregion and wetland type")
```

### EPA ecoregions: sampled and unsampled

New York has nine EPA Level III ecoregions. Sites cover four. Wetlands in the
other five are the **unlabeled** case in this notebook: no model can estimate
an ecoregion-specific mean there. The areas below are total land area. The
wetland area in each ecoregion (from the production maps) is what will weight
the upscaled estimate.

```{r eco-coverage}
eco_poly <- st_read(ECO_GPKG, quiet = TRUE)
stopifnot(all(levels(dat$Ecoregion) %in% eco_poly$US_L3NAME))

eco_coverage <- eco_poly |>
  mutate(area_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(geom)) / 1e6) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(US_L3CODE, US_L3NAME) |>
  summarise(area_km2 = sum(area_km2), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(count(dat, US_L3NAME = as.character(Ecoregion), name = "sites"),
            by = "US_L3NAME") |>
  mutate(sites = coalesce(sites, 0L),
         sampled = sites > 0,
         area_share = area_km2 / sum(area_km2)) |>
  arrange(desc(sampled), desc(area_km2))

kable(eco_coverage, digits = 3, caption = "EPA Level III ecoregions in New York")
cat(sprintf("Unsampled ecoregions: %.0f km² (%.1f%% of NY land area)\n",
            sum(eco_coverage$area_km2[!eco_coverage$sampled]),
            100 * sum(eco_coverage$area_share[!eco_coverage$sampled])))
```

### Response

CH4 is strongly right-skewed and includes a few small negative site means, so
it is modeled as log(CH4 + c). Iteration 1 found this gave the most normal
residuals of the transforms tried (raw, asinh, Gamma GLM).

```{r response}
ch4_shift <- abs(min(dat$CH4)) + SHIFT_ADD
dat <- dat |> mutate(CH4_resp = log(CH4 + ch4_shift))

## Back-transform from the model scale to flux. Gives the median flux, not the
## mean; the mean correction is handled with uncertainty in the next notebook.
back <- function(v) exp(v) - ch4_shift

cat(sprintf("Shift c = %.4f; %d of 48 site means are negative\n",
            ch4_shift, sum(dat$CH4 < 0)))
```

```{r response-plot, fig.height=4}
ggplot(dat, aes(Ecoregion, CH4_resp, color = Ecoregion)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5, color = "#898781") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, size = 2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 3.5,
               fill = "white", color = "black") +
  scale_color_manual(values = ECO_COLS, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Site-mean CH4 by ecoregion (model scale)",
       subtitle = "Diamond = ecoregion mean",
       x = NULL, y = "log(CH4 + c)")
```

### Covariate collinearity

```{r pred-check}
z_cov <- paste0("z_", names(COVARIATES))

cor(dat[names(COVARIATES)], method = "spearman") |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Spearman ρ among the covariates")

## Do the covariates differ by ecoregion? If strongly, ecoregion and the
## covariates compete for the same variance in the complex model.
dat |>
  group_by(Ecoregion) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(COVARIATES)), median), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Covariate medians by ecoregion")
```

## 2. Model fits

All models use the same response and data. `lm()` fits are used where there
is no random effect. Random-effect models are fit by REML for their
estimates, and by ML (`REML = FALSE`) wherever AIC is compared with an `lm()`
fit.

| Model | Formula | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `null` | `CH4_resp ~ 1` | reference |
| `eco_fixed` | `CH4_resp ~ Ecoregion` | upscaling candidate |
| `eco_random` | `CH4_resp ~ 1 + (1 \| Ecoregion)` | upscaling candidate |
| `complex_fixed` | `CH4_resp ~ Ecoregion + WETprob × DMV_sd + GEO_modefrac` | reported model |
| `complex_random` | `CH4_resp ~ WETprob × DMV_sd + GEO_modefrac + (1 \| Ecoregion)` | reported model, random-ecoregion version |
| `covariates` | `CH4_resp ~ WETprob × DMV_sd + GEO_modefrac` | what the covariates explain without ecoregion |

```{r formulas}
cov_terms <- "z_WETprob_mean * z_DMV_sd + z_GEO_modefrac"

FORMULAS <- list(
  null           = CH4_resp ~ 1,
  eco_fixed      = CH4_resp ~ Ecoregion,
  eco_random     = CH4_resp ~ 1 + (1 | Ecoregion),
  complex_fixed  = as.formula(paste("CH4_resp ~ Ecoregion +", cov_terms)),
  complex_random = as.formula(paste("CH4_resp ~", cov_terms, "+ (1 | Ecoregion)")),
  covariates     = as.formula(paste("CH4_resp ~", cov_terms))
)

is_mixed <- function(f) any(grepl("|", deparse(f), fixed = TRUE))

## REML = TRUE for estimates; FALSE for likelihood / AIC comparisons with lm
fit_model <- function(f, d, REML = TRUE) {
  if (is_mixed(f)) lmer(f, data = d, REML = REML) else lm(f, data = d)
}

fits <- map(FORMULAS, fit_model, d = dat)
fits_ml <- map(FORMULAS, fit_model, d = dat, REML = FALSE)
```

## 3. Ecoregion only: fixed vs. random

### 3.1 Fits

```{r eco-fits}
summary(fits$eco_fixed)
anova(fits$null, fits$eco_fixed)

summary(fits$eco_random)
```

### 3.2 Is there between-ecoregion variance?

The ecoregion variance (τ²) is estimated from **only 4 levels**, so it is
poorly determined. The ML estimate is biased low with this few groups, so
REML is shown too. The profile interval shows the range of τ values the data
are consistent with. It is a check on whether τ can be estimated at all, not
an uncertainty estimate for upscaling.

```{r eco-variance}
vc_tbl <- function(m, label) {
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m))
  tibble(fit = label,
         tau2_ecoregion = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Ecoregion"],
         sigma2_residual = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "Residual"],
         ICC = tau2_ecoregion / (tau2_ecoregion + sigma2_residual))
}
bind_rows(vc_tbl(fits$eco_random, "REML"), vc_tbl(fits_ml$eco_random, "ML")) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Variance components of eco_random")

## Profile CI for the SDs (.sig01 = tau, .sigma = residual SD)
tau_ci <- confint(fits$eco_random, parm = ".sig01", method = "profile", quiet = TRUE)
kable(tau_ci, digits = 3, caption = "Profile 95% interval for the ecoregion SD τ")

## LRT of tau^2 = 0: on the boundary, so halve the chi-square p-value
lrt <- as.numeric(2 * (logLik(fits_ml$eco_random) - logLik(fits_ml$null)))
cat(sprintf("LRT for (1 | Ecoregion) vs null: chi2 = %.2f, boundary-corrected p = %.3f\n",
            lrt, 0.5 * pchisq(lrt, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)))
```

### 3.3 Ecoregion estimates: fixed means vs. shrunken random effects

With a fixed effect, each ecoregion gets its own sample mean. With a random
effect, each ecoregion mean is pulled toward the overall mean by the factor
τ² / (τ² + σ²/n), where n = 12 sites per ecoregion. Ecoregions with a weaker
signal are pulled further.

The **unlabeled** row is the prediction for wetlands in the five unsampled EPA
ecoregions:

* `eco_random`: the population intercept (the random effect set to 0). This
  is what the model is built to predict for a new group.
* `eco_fixed`: no coefficient exists. The closest equivalent is the
  equal-weight average of the four ecoregion means. Because the design is
  balanced (12 per ecoregion), this equals the overall sample mean.

So the **point predictions** for unlabeled areas are nearly the same under
either model. The real difference is in the uncertainty. The random-effect
model carries τ² into the prediction for a new ecoregion. The fixed-effect
model has no basis for that term. This is picked up in the uncertainty
notebook.

```{r eco-estimates}
eco_lv <- levels(dat$Ecoregion)
nd_eco <- tibble(Ecoregion = factor(eco_lv, levels = eco_lv))

shrink_tbl <- dat |>
  group_by(Ecoregion) |>
  summarise(n = n(), sample_mean = mean(CH4_resp), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(fixed = predict(fits$eco_fixed, nd_eco),
         random = predict(fits$eco_random, nd_eco),
         grand = fixef(fits$eco_random)[["(Intercept)"]],
         shrinkage = 1 - (random - grand) / (sample_mean - grand)) |>
  select(-grand) |>
  mutate(Ecoregion = as.character(Ecoregion)) |>
  add_row(Ecoregion = "Unlabeled (new ecoregion)", n = 0L, sample_mean = NA,
          fixed = mean(predict(fits$eco_fixed, nd_eco)),
          random = predict(fits$eco_random, tibble(Ecoregion = "new"),
                           allow.new.levels = TRUE),
          shrinkage = NA) |>
  mutate(fixed_flux = back(fixed), random_flux = back(random))

kable(shrink_tbl, digits = 3,
      caption = paste("Ecoregion predictions, model scale and back-transformed",
                      "(median flux, same units as CH4_avg). shrinkage = fraction of the",
                      "distance from the overall mean removed by the random effect"))
```

```{r eco-estimates-plot, fig.height=4}
shrink_tbl |>
  select(Ecoregion, sample_mean, fixed, random) |>
  pivot_longer(c(fixed, random), names_to = "model", values_to = "estimate") |>
  mutate(Ecoregion = factor(Ecoregion, levels = rev(shrink_tbl$Ecoregion))) |>
  ggplot(aes(estimate, Ecoregion, color = model, shape = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = fixef(fits$eco_random)[["(Intercept)"]], color = "#c3c2b7",
             linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(fixed = "#2a78d6", random = "#eb6834")) +
  labs(title = "Ecoregion estimates: fixed effect vs. random effect (model scale)",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = population intercept of eco_random",
       x = "log(CH4 + c)", y = NULL, color = NULL, shape = NULL)
```

## 4. Complex model

### 4.1 Fits

```{r complex-fits}
summary(fits$complex_fixed)
summary(fits$complex_random)
summary(fits$covariates)

## Does each block add to the other? (lm fits, nested F-tests)
anova(fits$eco_fixed, fits$complex_fixed)   # covariates given ecoregion
anova(fits$covariates, fits$complex_fixed)  # ecoregion given covariates
```

### 4.2 Coefficients

```{r coefs, fig.height=4.5}
## Fixed-effect estimates with 95% Wald CIs, one row per term per model
coef_table <- function(models) {
  imap_dfr(models, function(m, nm) {
    est <- if (inherits(m, "merMod")) fixef(m) else coef(m)
    ci <- if (inherits(m, "merMod")) confint(m, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald") else confint(m)
    tibble(model = nm, term = names(est), estimate = unname(est),
           lo = ci[names(est), 1], hi = ci[names(est), 2])
  }) |>
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
    mutate(term = gsub("z_", "", term),
           term = factor(term, levels = rev(unique(term))),
           model = factor(model, levels = names(models)))
}

coef_table(fits[c("complex_fixed", "complex_random", "covariates")]) |>
  ggplot(aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, color = "#898781") +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, color = "#2a78d6") +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  labs(title = "Complex model coefficients",
       subtitle = "95% CIs. Covariates per 1 SD; ecoregion terms relative to the first level",
       x = "Estimate (log scale; exp(b) = multiplicative change)", y = NULL)
```

### 4.3 The WETprob × DMV_sd interaction

WETprob is bunched near 1 and DMV_sd is right-skewed (a few sites with very
high microtopographic variability). Both of these mean a handful of sites can
drive the interaction. The Cook's distance table in 4.4 shows which ones.

```{r int-plot, fig.height=5}
## Predicted CH4 vs DMV_sd at low / median / high WETprob (10th, 50th, 90th
## percentiles), GEO_modefrac at its mean, averaged over ecoregions
## (equal weight). Back-transformed: median flux.
q_wet <- quantile(dat$z_WETprob_mean, c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))
grid <- crossing(z_DMV_sd = seq(min(dat$z_DMV_sd), max(dat$z_DMV_sd), length.out = 60),
                 z_WETprob_mean = q_wet,
                 Ecoregion = factor(eco_lv, levels = eco_lv)) |>
  mutate(z_GEO_modefrac = 0)
grid$fit <- predict(fits$complex_fixed, grid)
grid <- grid |>
  group_by(z_DMV_sd, z_WETprob_mean) |>
  summarise(fit = mean(fit), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(DMV_sd = z_DMV_sd * sd(dat$DMV_sd) + mean(dat$DMV_sd),
         level = factor(z_WETprob_mean, levels = q_wet,
                        labels = sprintf("%s WETprob (%.2f)", c("Low", "Median", "High"),
                                         q_wet * sd(dat$WETprob_mean) + mean(dat$WETprob_mean))))

ggplot(grid, aes(DMV_sd, back(fit))) +
  geom_point(data = dat, aes(DMV_sd, CH4, fill = WETprob_mean), shape = 21,
             color = "white", size = 2.4, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_line(aes(color = level, linetype = level), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#2a78d6", "#898781", "#eb6834")) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#e1e0d9", high = "#1f4e8c", name = "Observed WETprob") +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.01),
                     breaks = c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10)) +
  labs(title = "complex_fixed: predicted CH4 vs DMV SD at low, median and high WETprob",
       subtitle = "GEO_modefrac at its mean; averaged over ecoregions; points = observed site means",
       x = "DMV_sd (10 m)", y = "CH4 flux (pseudo-log axis)",
       color = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

### 4.4 Diagnostics

```{r diag, fig.height=7}
diag_models <- fits[c("eco_fixed", "eco_random", "complex_fixed", "complex_random")]

d <- imap_dfr(diag_models, \(m, nm) tibble(
  model = nm, fitted = fitted(m), resid = residuals(m),
  Wetland_Type = dat$Wetland_Type
)) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = names(diag_models)))

rf <- ggplot(d, aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(aes(color = Wetland_Type, shape = Wetland_Type), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = WT_COLS) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = WT_SHAPES) +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs fitted", x = "Fitted", y = "Residual",
       color = "Wetland type", shape = "Wetland type")
qq <- ggplot(d, aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "#c3c2b7") +
  stat_qq(size = 1.6, color = "#2a78d6") +
  facet_wrap(~model, nrow = 1) +
  labs(title = "Residual normal Q-Q", x = "Theoretical", y = "Sample")
rf / qq
```

Wetland type is not in any model, because the production maps have no wetland
classes. Colouring the residuals by type shows whether ecoregion and the
covariates already capture the differences between types.

```{r influence}
## Influential sites in the complex model (Cook's D > 4/n is the usual flag)
tibble(Site_ID = dat$Site_ID, Ecoregion = dat$Ecoregion,
       WETprob_mean = dat$WETprob_mean, DMV_sd = dat$DMV_sd,
       GEO_modefrac = dat$GEO_modefrac, CH4 = dat$CH4,
       cooks_d = cooks.distance(fits$complex_fixed),
       leverage = hatvalues(fits$complex_fixed)) |>
  arrange(desc(cooks_d)) |>
  filter(cooks_d > 4 / nrow(dat)) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "complex_fixed: sites with Cook's D > 4/n")
```

### 4.5 Sensitivity: the most influential site and the scale of DMV_sd

Two checks on whether the interaction is a general pattern or the work of a
few sites. Both refit `complex_fixed` and report in-sample R² and LOO cvR²
(Section 5 explains cvR²):

* **Drop the site with the largest Cook's D.**
* **Use log(DMV_sd)** in place of DMV_sd, which pulls in the long right tail.

```{r sensitivity}
top_site <- dat$Site_ID[which.max(cooks.distance(fits$complex_fixed))]

sens_fit <- function(d, label) {
  m <- lm(FORMULAS$complex_fixed, data = d)
  folds <- seq_len(nrow(d))
  pred <- base <- numeric(nrow(d))
  for (i in folds) {
    tr <- droplevels(d[-i, ])
    pred[i] <- predict(lm(FORMULAS$complex_fixed, data = tr), d[i, ]) # ecoregion always in training
    base[i] <- mean(tr$CH4_resp)
  }
  tibble(variant = label, n = nrow(d), R2 = summary(m)$r.squared,
         cvR2_LOO = 1 - sum((d$CH4_resp - pred)^2) / sum((d$CH4_resp - base)^2),
         `WETprob:DMV_sd` = coef(m)[["z_WETprob_mean:z_DMV_sd"]],
         `p (interaction)` = summary(m)$coefficients["z_WETprob_mean:z_DMV_sd", 4])
}

bind_rows(
  sens_fit(dat, "as specified"),
  sens_fit(filter(dat, Site_ID != top_site), paste("without", top_site)),
  sens_fit(mutate(dat, z_DMV_sd = as.numeric(scale(log(DMV_sd)))), "log(DMV_sd)")
) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "complex_fixed sensitivity (interaction on the z scale of each variant)")
```

## 5. Model comparison: in-sample and cross-validated

In-sample fit tells you how much of the 48-site variation a model accounts
for. The upscaling question is how well it predicts **sites it was not fit
to**. Three cross-validation schemes, from easiest to hardest:

* **Leave one site out (LOO).** The held-out site's ecoregion is in the
  training data. This is like predicting an unsampled wetland in a sampled
  ecoregion.
* **Spatial blocks.** Sites within `r CV_BLOCK_KM` km of each other are held
  out together, so nearby, similar sites can't stand in for each other.
* **Leave one ecoregion out (LOEO).** All 12 sites of an ecoregion are held
  out. This is the **unlabeled-area** case. Random-effect models predict the
  population mean. Fixed-ecoregion models have no coefficient for the
  held-out ecoregion, so they predict with the equal-weight average over the
  three training ecoregions (Section 3.3).

Predictive R² = 1 − SSE / SS, where SS uses the **training-fold mean** as
the baseline prediction. It can be negative: ≤ 0 means the model predicts
held-out sites no better than the mean of the training sites. Standardizing
covariates on all 48 sites does not leak information between folds, because
a linear model's fitted values don't depend on how its covariates are
centered or scaled.

```{r cv-fn}
## Predict new sites. Random-effect models use the ecoregion BLUP when the
## ecoregion was in training and the population mean otherwise. Fixed-ecoregion
## lm models average predictions over the training ecoregions when the
## ecoregion is new.
predict_new <- function(m, newdata) {
  newdata$Ecoregion <- as.character(newdata$Ecoregion)
  if (inherits(m, "merMod")) {
    return(unname(predict(m, newdata = newdata, allow.new.levels = TRUE)))
  }
  lv <- m$xlevels$Ecoregion
  if (is.null(lv)) return(unname(predict(m, newdata)))
  known <- newdata$Ecoregion %in% lv
  out <- numeric(nrow(newdata))
  if (any(known)) out[known] <- predict(m, newdata[known, , drop = FALSE])
  if (any(!known)) {
    out[!known] <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(lv, \(l) {
      predict(m, mutate(newdata[!known, , drop = FALSE], Ecoregion = l))
    })) / length(lv)
  }
  out
}

FOLDS <- list(
  LOO = seq_len(nrow(dat)),
  spatial = cutree(hclust(dist(dat[c("x", "y")]) / 1000, method = "complete"),
                   h = CV_BLOCK_KM),
  LOEO = as.integer(dat$Ecoregion)
)

cv_predict <- function(f, folds) {
  pred <- base <- numeric(nrow(dat))
  for (k in unique(folds)) {
    test <- folds == k
    train <- droplevels(dat[!test, ])
    m <- suppressMessages(fit_model(f, train))
    pred[test] <- predict_new(m, dat[test, ])
    base[test] <- mean(train$CH4_resp)
  }
  tibble(Site_ID = dat$Site_ID, obs = dat$CH4_resp, pred = pred, base = base)
}

pred_r2 <- function(obs, pred, base) 1 - sum((obs - pred)^2) / sum((obs - base)^2)

imap_dfr(FOLDS, \(f, nm) tibble(scheme = nm, folds = n_distinct(f),
                                min_held_out = min(table(f)),
                                max_held_out = max(table(f)))) |>
  kable(caption = "Cross-validation folds")
```

```{r cv-run}
cv_res <- map(FORMULAS, \(f) map(FOLDS, \(fo) cv_predict(f, fo)))
```

```{r comparison}
r2_in <- function(m) {
  if (inherits(m, "merMod")) {
    r <- suppressWarnings(r.squaredGLMM(m))
    c(R2_marginal = unname(r[1, "R2m"]), R2_conditional = unname(r[1, "R2c"]))
  } else {
    r <- summary(m)$r.squared
    c(R2_marginal = r, R2_conditional = r)
  }
}

comparison <- imap_dfr(FORMULAS, function(f, nm) {
  r2 <- r2_in(fits[[nm]])
  cv <- map_dbl(cv_res[[nm]], \(p) pred_r2(p$obs, p$pred, p$base))
  tibble(model = nm,
         k = attr(logLik(fits_ml[[nm]]), "df"),
         AICc = AICc(fits_ml[[nm]]),
         R2_marginal = r2[["R2_marginal"]],
         R2_conditional = r2[["R2_conditional"]],
         adj_R2 = if (inherits(fits[[nm]], "lm")) summary(fits[[nm]])$adj.r.squared else NA,
         cvR2_LOO = cv[["LOO"]], cvR2_spatial = cv[["spatial"]], cvR2_LOEO = cv[["LOEO"]],
         cvRMSE_LOO = sqrt(mean((cv_res[[nm]]$LOO$obs - cv_res[[nm]]$LOO$pred)^2)))
}) |>
  mutate(dAICc = AICc - min(AICc), .after = AICc)

kable(comparison, digits = 3,
      caption = paste("Model comparison on the model (log) scale. AICc from ML fits.",
                      "R2_marginal = fixed effects only; R2_conditional adds the ecoregion",
                      "random effect (equal to R2 for lm fits)"))
```

How to read the R² columns for the random-effect models:

* `eco_random` has no fixed effects, so its marginal R² is 0. Its conditional
  R² is the share explained by the shrunken ecoregion means, which is the
  comparable number to `eco_fixed`'s R².
* The CV columns are directly comparable across all models. In LOO and
  spatial CV, random-effect models use the ecoregion BLUP. In LOEO, every
  model predicts a new ecoregion.

```{r cv-plot, fig.height=6}
cv_long <- imap_dfr(cv_res, \(by_scheme, nm) bind_rows(by_scheme, .id = "scheme") |>
                      mutate(model = nm)) |>
  left_join(select(dat, Site_ID, Ecoregion), by = "Site_ID") |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = names(FORMULAS)),
         scheme = factor(scheme, levels = names(FOLDS)))

cv_long |>
  filter(model != "null") |>
  ggplot(aes(pred, obs, color = Ecoregion)) +
  geom_abline(color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  facet_grid(scheme ~ model) +
  scale_color_manual(values = ECO_COLS) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Cross-validated predictions vs observed (model scale)",
       x = "Predicted log(CH4 + c)", y = "Observed log(CH4 + c)", color = NULL)
```

## 6. Predictions for unlabeled areas

These are the point predictions each model would give for a wetland in one of
the five unsampled EPA ecoregions (Section 1). For the complex models the covariates are set to
their sample means (z = 0). The random-effect versions predict from the
population intercept. The fixed versions average over the four ecoregions.

```{r unlabeled}
nd_new <- tibble(Ecoregion = "Unlabeled", z_WETprob_mean = 0, z_DMV_sd = 0,
                 z_GEO_modefrac = 0)
imap_dfr(fits[c("eco_fixed", "eco_random", "complex_fixed", "complex_random")],
         \(m, nm) tibble(model = nm, model_scale = predict_new(m, nd_new))) |>
  mutate(flux_median = back(model_scale)) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Prediction for an unlabeled area (covariates at their means)")
```

## 7. Spatial autocorrelation in residuals

If nearby sites have similar residuals, the model's standard errors are too
small, and the spatial CV in Section 5 will be worse than LOO. Moran's I is
tested with 999 permutations (one-sided, testing for positive
autocorrelation). Neighbours are site pairs within `r NEIGHBOUR_KM` km.

```{r moran}
dist_km <- as.matrix(dist(dat[c("x", "y")])) / 1000

moran_I <- function(r, w) {
  z <- r - mean(r)
  length(r) / sum(w) * sum(w * outer(z, z)) / sum(z^2)
}
moran_test <- function(r, w, nsim = 999) {
  obs <- moran_I(r, w)
  sims <- replicate(nsim, moran_I(sample(r), w))
  tibble(I = obs, expected = -1 / (length(r) - 1),
         p = (sum(sims >= obs) + 1) / (nsim + 1))
}

w_band <- (dist_km <= NEIGHBOUR_KM) * 1
diag(w_band) <- 0
cat(sum(w_band) / 2, "site pairs within", NEIGHBOUR_KM, "km;",
    sum(rowSums(w_band) > 0), "of 48 sites have at least one neighbour\n")

map_dfr(fits[c("null", "eco_fixed", "eco_random", "complex_fixed", "complex_random")],
        \(m) moran_test(residuals(m), w_band), .id = "model") |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("Moran's I of residuals, neighbours within %d km",
                                      NEIGHBOUR_KM))
```

```{r resid-map, fig.height=5}
imap_dfr(fits[c("eco_fixed", "complex_fixed")],
         \(m, nm) tibble(model = nm, x = dat$x, y = dat$y,
                         resid_z = as.numeric(scale(residuals(m))))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x / 1000, y / 1000, fill = resid_z)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, color = "white", stroke = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2a78d6", mid = "#f0efec", high = "#e34948",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-2.5, 2.5), oob = scales::squish,
                       name = "Residual (SD)") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Residuals in space", subtitle = "Colour capped at ±2.5 SD",
       x = "Easting (km, EPSG:6347)", y = "Northing (km)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

## 8. Summary and next steps

How to read the results:

* **Fixed vs. random ecoregion (upscaling model).** Compare `eco_fixed` and
  `eco_random` on dAICc, LOO cvR² and LOEO cvR². In sampled ecoregions the two
  differ only by the shrinkage in Section 3.3. In unlabeled areas their point
  predictions are almost the same (the overall mean). The argument for the
  random effect is mainly that it gives a principled prediction **and a
  variance** (τ²) for a new ecoregion. Note the caveat that τ² comes from only
  4 ecoregions.
* **Complex model (reported alongside).** In-sample R² vs. cross-validated R²
  shows how much of the complex model's apparent advantage holds for new
  sites. The gap between LOO and LOEO shows how much of it depends on knowing
  the ecoregion.

3. **Area.** Wetland area per EPA ecoregion as Σ WETprob × pixel area from the
